events.title: Boston Tea Party
events.description: Colonists, many disguised as Mohawk Indians, boarded three British ships in Boston Harbor and dumped 342 chests of tea into the water to protest the Tea Act and taxation without representation.
events.significance: The protest escalated tensions between Britain and its American colonies, prompting the punitive Coercive Acts and helping set the stage for the American Revolution.

events.title: Birth of Ludwig van Beethoven (baptized)
events.description: Ludwig van Beethoven was baptized in Bonn on December 17, 1770; his birth date is traditionally celebrated on December 16. He became one of the most influential composers in Western music.
events.significance: Beethoven bridged the Classical and Romantic eras, and his symphonies, sonatas, and quartets remain cornerstones of the classical repertoire.

events.title: Battle of the Bulge Begins
events.description: Germany launched a massive surprise offensive through the Ardennes Forest in Belgium and Luxembourg, aiming to split Allied lines and capture the port of Antwerp.
events.significance: It was the largest and bloodiest single battle fought by the U.S. in WWII; the failure of the offensive exhausted German reserves and hastened the end of the war in Europe.

events.title: Surrender of Pakistani Forces and Creation of Bangladesh
events.description: Pakistani forces in East Pakistan surrendered to the joint Indian and Bangladeshi forces in Dhaka, ending the Bangladesh Liberation War after the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.
events.significance: The surrender led to the independence of Bangladesh as a sovereign nation and reshaped the political landscape of South Asia.

events.title: Birth of Jane Austen
events.description: English novelist Jane Austen was born in Steventon, Hampshire, and went on to write novels such as Pride and Prejudice, Emma, and Sense and Sensibility.
events.significance: Austen's works of social commentary and wit became enduring classics of English literature and continue to be widely read and adapted.
